leaves.doc: Bump-Friedberg-Hoffstein, Invent. Math. 102 (1990) 543-618, opening theorem (pp. 543-544), clause (ii), at weight 2 and trivial character: for f a newform of weight 2 and trivial character on Gamma_0(N), epsilon the sign of the functional equation of the completed L(s, f) at level N (IsFESign, over ZInQ.Literature.completedL), and S a finite set of primes containing the primes dividing 2N, there is a fundamental discriminant d != 1 (Int.IsFundamentalDiscr, Mathlib) with epsilon d > 0, every p in S split in Q(sqrt d) (two distinct primes of O_K above p, K a quadratic number field containing sqrt d), and L(1, f, chi_d) != 0 (FHPrinted.CentralValueNeZero, chi_d from its local components)
leaves.flag: unread: BFH 1990 opening theorem clause (ii) read by the theorem-application audit from page images of pp. 543-544 (docs/theorem-application-audit/evidence/theta-upstream.md, INVENTORY.md A025), not by this task (no copy on the host); three checks for the reading: (1) no CM exclusion (the use applies it to the CM newform of C_d); (2) no condition on the level (the use has N = 32 d^2, even and not squarefree); (3) the wording of clause (ii) (fundamental discriminant or squarefree d; 'split' or a congruence class modulo 4N). If (1) or (2) fails the print does not cover the use; if (3) reads 'squarefree' or a congruence class the leaf is a consequence (small dictionary), not the printed form
